title: wb claim admits only ST addresses, so issue and maintenance work can never be claimed
body:
`is_claim_address` (native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/model.rs:148) admits exactly two shapes:

    None => is_thread_id(claim),
    Some((thread, seq)) => is_thread_id(thread) && seq.len() == 2 && seq.chars().all(..is_ascii_digit)

and `is_thread_id` requires literally ST followed by digits. `Facade::wb_claim` (facade.rs:7995) is the only write door and refuses anything else by name.

It never calls `is_issue_id`, which exists at model.rs:176. So a session working intent/issues/0505 cannot say so on its board -- even though `organize --default` already declares open issues as ISSUE:<NNNN> lines in .intentfiles, so this is an address kind the system writes down elsewhere and will not accept here.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT `claims:` IS EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION FOR EXACTLY THE WORK THAT FILLS THE TIME BETWEEN RELEASES, and it is therefore silent precisely where two concurrent sessions would collide. Measured 2026-09-22: all five Intent nodes carry `claims: []`, and the five most recent commits were hook adoption, a CI workflow fix and three whiteboard folds -- none of them claimable, so none of them claimed. The field is not under-used; it is unreachable for that work.

THIS IS A DESIGN QUESTION RATHER THAN A WIDENING. `st renumber` rewrites every board claim on a thread or its packages, and `wb unclaim` deliberately does not validate and removes by value; both assume a claim is a resolvable address. Admitting a second address kind needs a decision about what those verbs do with one. Admitting free text needs a decision about how two claims are compared for collision at all.

PROVENANCE. Recorded on devbin's cc whiteboard 2026-08-28, carried unverified for 25 days, re-verified against Intent at 23d431f7e on 2026-09-22. The exclusion of ISSUES is sharper than the original record, which named only maintenance work.

RESOLVED on hv's decision 29. A board claims an issue as `ISSUE:0512`, the manifest's own spelling. vc judged the bank: blob f8f2cc41b9d507c34be1926f6f2611ac53670005, patch-id e3ab4461fd9733537292b3fae57a5c92c39e54ae, seven files +205 -16. `intentsvcs` RC=0 (301 lib, 1529 suite, 4 ignored); `intent-cli` RC=0 (742).

THE WIDENING IS FOUR LINES AND THE WORK IS ITS CONSEQUENCES. `renumber::issue` gained the claim rewriting `renumber::thread` already had, because admitting issue claims falsified that function's stated reason for rewriting nothing. Driven as a control with the model widened and the renumber left alone: `left: ["ISSUE:0021"], right: ["ISSUE:0022"]` -- a board still claiming a number that had moved, at exit 0, with nothing reporting it. The fixture carries a second board claiming a different issue which must stay put, without which a renumber rewriting every claim in sight would pass.

`wb migrate` is widened by construction and that was CONFIRMED by reading both call sites (`wbmigrate.rs:237` and `:244`) rather than trusted from the comment saying so.

THE RULE HAD THREE HOMES TEACHING IT, not the one remedy named in this issue: `facade.rs:2218`, `wbmigrate.rs:250` in its own independent words, and `surface/dispatch-table.json`, whose row generates CLI help and the MCP tool schema and is therefore read BEFORE any refusal. The two prose remedies remaining independent of each other is filed separately.

THE ARG TYPE became `claim-address` for `wb claim` and `wb unclaim`, rather than widening the shared `st-id[/NN]`, which eight other verbs use -- widening it would have told `st start` and `wp done` they accept an issue. `wb unclaim` needed it although it never validates: it removes by value, so it would have accepted an issue anyway, but an agent told the argument is a steel thread id never tries, and you could have claimed an issue with no way to learn how to drop it.
